records.title: Learning the effective order of a hypergraph dynamical system
records.sourceVersion: arXiv 2306.01813v1 2023-06-02 as read; final Science Advances 10(19) May 2024 uses shifted definition numbering, check before quoting published text.

definitions.name: dynamical order

definitions.name: effective order
definitions.formal: p_min=minimal hyperedge order preserving described system; p_min ≤ min(k,p_dyn), with equalities under additional example-specific conditions

equations.expression: (1) dot x_i=Σ_{E∋i} sin[Σ_{j∈E}(x_j-x_i)]; (2) dot x_i=Σ_{E∋i}Σ_{j∈E}sin(x_j-x_i)=Σ_j(B^T B)_{ij}sin(x_j-x_i); (3) B_{Ei}=1_{i∈E}
equations.meaning: Same nontrivial hypergraph incidence may support irreducible joint hyperedge update or exactly reducible pairwise dynamics depending on source interaction function.
Types and event-edge group are given; dynamics functional form on simultaneous source values

equations.locator: Preprint p.4 Definition 2 Eq.(5), Definition 3 Eq.(7)
equations.meaning: Explicit reducibility/factorization test; observed max hyperedge size does not imply irreducible physical dynamical order.

records.title: Encoding reaction systems in Petri nets
records.sourceVersion: Natural Computing 25, article 8, published 14 February 2026 (version of record), original full text read.

definitions.name: reaction
definitions.formal: r-system ℛ=(S,A), finite S; each a=(R,I,P) with R,I,P nonempty subsets of S and R∩I=∅

definitions.name: enabled
definitions.formal: a enabled in U⊆S iff R⊆U and I∩U=∅

definitions.name: parallel deterministic update
definitions.formal: res_A(U)=⋃_{a∈A enabled at U} P_a; all enabled reactions at U are executed, no one-event scheduler

equations.expression: PT-net N=(P,T,F,M0), pre(t)⊂P and post(t)⊂P, t enabled at M if M(p)≥1 for every p∈pre(t)
equations.meaning: Token-transition semantics is not identical to set-level reaction semantics.
Higher-order positive reactant conjunction plus explicit negative inhibitor guard and concurrent production.

equations.locator: Section 3 Encoding I Eqs.(3),(4), Theorem 1 clauses (2),(3)
equations.expression: pre(v_U)={p_start},post(v_U)={p_U}; pre(t_U)={p_U},post(t_U)={p_res_A(U)}; initialized Petri firing sequence projects to r-system sequence and conversely.
equations.meaning: Exact forward/back history correspondence for the stated 1-safe encoding, but the encoding uses an extra place for every U⊆S.

records.transition: Synchronous/parallel update U→res_A(U), translated to Petri firing sequences with selected encoding and exact mapping
sourceAssumptions: fixed finite S
entities not automatically persistent: only products survive if re-produced
source reactions generally parallel at each step

records.falsifier: Proposed native→Petri map cannot represent distinct source-edge occurrence multiplicity, Hamming-weight enabling, or T4 asymmetric conflicts/triple blocking without additional typed control state.

records.title: Rule Algebras for Adhesive Categories
records.sourceVersion: Computer Science Logic 2018 published original proceedings PDF, 21 pages; distinguish later journal/LMCS version and arXiv/abstract aliases.

definitions.name: adhesive category
definitions.formal: category C has pullbacks, pushouts along monos and those pushouts form van Kampen squares, Def. 2.1

definitions.name: linear DPO production
definitions.formal: span L<-l-K-r->R with mono l and r, Def. 2.2; admissible monic match m:L↪C satisfying gluing/pushout complement (Def. 2.3,2.6)

definitions.name: dependency overlap
definitions.formal: span of monos R1<-X12->L2 with required pushout complements (Sec. 3 Eq.4)

equations.locator: PDF p2 Definition 2.2 Eq.(1) and p3 Def 2.6 Eq.(3)
equations.expression: L←K→R; admissible match m:L↪C yields double pushout C ⇒_{p,m} D, unique up to isomorphism
equations.meaning: DPO source category and exact gluing/match admissibility define lawful event step.

equations.expression: Concurrent composition p2 ▷_m p1 from overlap m; valid two-step derivation C⇒_{p}⇒_{q} is represented by a composite admissible rule, producing isomorphic result.
equations.meaning: Theorem composes admissible matched source rewrites, not arbitrary overlapping events.

equations.expression: For admissibly corresponding match pairs, p3▷(p2▷p1)=(p3▷p2)▷p1
equations.meaning: Associativity holds via bijection of *admissible match data*, not initial pairwise commuting of all standalone firings.

records.title: Classical sequential growth dynamics for causal sets
records.sourceVersion: arXiv gr-qc/9904062v3 dated June 2004, PRD 61 024002 appeared 1999/2000, original arXiv paper text and pages 8–11 inspected.

definitions.name: internal temporality
definitions.formal: new causet element born to future of, or unrelated to, existing elements; cannot be added to past (PDF p.9)

definitions.name: discrete general covariance
definitions.formal: product of transition probabilities along paths from empty causet to same unlabeled finite causet agrees for any allowed birth order (PDF p.9)

definitions.name: Bell causality for transitions
definitions.formal: ratio of two child transition probabilities in causet C equals ratio of corresponding probabilities after removing spectator elements, for nonzero probabilities (PDF p.10 Eq.2)

equations.locator: PDF p.9 discrete general covariance paragraph
equations.expression: For paths γ1,γ2 from ∅ to same unlabeled causet C: ∏_{t∈γ1}p(t)=∏_{t∈γ2}p(t)
equations.meaning: Gauge-independent sequential birth probability is a postulated criterion, not generally implied by any graph rewrite.

equations.expression: Pr(C→C1)/Pr(C→C2) = Pr(B→B1)/Pr(B→B2) for B=union of two precursor sets, after deleting spectators
equations.meaning: Conditional probability ratio uses explicit causal ancestors; requires well-defined stochastic transition probabilities and nonzero case.

equations.locator: PDF p.11 onward Markov sum rule
equations.expression: Σ_{distinct allowed child transitions from C} Pr(C→Ci) = 1 (with appropriate multiplicities/possible transition equivalences)
equations.meaning: Transition probabilities obey specific Markov normalization and general covariance.

modelObjects: stochastic transition weight and unlabeled isomorphism classes
records.transition: One poset element added to future of chosen precursor with postulated Markov transition probabilities satisfying internal temporality, Bell causality and general covariance.
sourceAssumptions: binary locally finite partial order fundamental, not native k-ary event occurrence multiset
stochastic Markov transition kernel fundamental
new element birth postulated; same host birth label is gauge
precursor past constraints and nonzero probabilities in Bell ratio
records.positiveStructuralLink: Exact benchmark for invariance of probabilities of equivalent birth-history orderings and conditional independence of uninvolved spectators.
records.nonfaithfulMappingRisk: T2 native raw FIFO/same-index random diverges under relabeling, and T4 has state-sensitive coenabled orders; cannot identify these with sequential-growth covariance without an exact quotient and stochastic law.
records.falsifier: No well-defined native stochastic Markov kernel invariant under tested occurrence transport, or intrinsic cause relation not represented by source hyperedge birth order.
records.newStructuralFamily: Stochastic path-covariance and spectator-independent transition ratios

records.title: What Are Higher-Order Networks?

definitions.name: hypergraph
definitions.formal: H=(V,E) with finite vertex set V and collection of nonempty subsets E, Definition 2.1; multiset incidence needs additional typed multiplicity bookkeeping

definitions.name: simplicial complex
definitions.formal: Every nonempty subset of a simplex must also be a simplex, Definition 2.3

definitions.name: generic joint dynamical influence
definitions.formal: dot x_k=F(x_k)+H_k(x), with H_k depending jointly on all node states; Eq.5.2

equations.expression: H=(V,E), E⊆P(V)\{∅}; simplicial K downward-closed: e∈K ⇒ any nonempty f⊆e is also in K
equations.meaning: Incidence and simplicial closure are different model inputs, not equivalent physics.

equations.expression: dot x_k=F(x_k)+H_k(x); formal expansion dot x_k=F(x_k)+Σ_j A_jk G_k(x_k,x_j)+Σ_{j,l} A^3_jlk G^3_k(x_k,x_j,x_l)+…
equations.meaning: A binary graph of dependencies can still permit nonlinear multiway dynamical interaction; formal higher-order decompositions need not be unique.

equations.expression: dot x_k=F(x_k)+ε Ĥ_k(x), with an attracting phase torus. Phase-reduced dynamics may contain effective nonpairwise terms even if original full-state coupling was additive/pairwise.
equations.meaning: Higher-order interaction appearance depends on observer/change of variables, not solely native microscopic arity.
